why: Only a rephrasing of the opening sentence.
The longer version spells out the 'maybe' framing of Mollick's question, which is just explanation.
'Curated library the agent checks first' is an analogy, so it is explanation.
'Module 5 builds the tools...' is a forward hint.
'Pushback rounds were the work' is emphasis and reflection, not an objection the room would raise.
The extra sentence tells the student how to read a mismatch, which is more explanation.
'It works. You watched it work.' is emphasis.
'Module 1 starts here; you'll use it everywhere' is a forward hint.
The extra text reveals the Finnish answer early and adds a 'before you watch' line, which is pacing rather than any of the three jobs.
'The model is good. It is still not 100% deterministic' is a closing restatement, with at most a trace of the 'bad model' objection.
'Compounding rules files are not tidy' is a restating closer.
'That's next module' is a forward hint.
The extra text only names the concept ('The wall') and rephrases the sentence. It doesn't orient the student, add a numeral, or answer a doubt.
'You don't need to get it right first time' answers the fear of getting it wrong, which students have but won't say aloud.
